<script>
  // Restore the saved color scheme preference, or
  // enact the browser preference if "automatic", 
  // without expecting DOM load to have completed.
  //
  // Also restore any saved readingmode and ToC display preferences.
  function initializeReadingPreferences() {
    let saved_theme = localStorage.getItem("ar5iv_theme") || "automatic";
    if (saved_theme === "automatic") {
      if (window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches) {
        saved_theme = "dark";
      }
    }
    if (saved_theme == "dark") {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "dark");
    } else {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "light");
    }

    const tocDisplay = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_toc_display');
    if (tocDisplay) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-toc-display", tocDisplay);
    }
    const readingMode = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_reading_mode');
    if (readingMode) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-reading-mode", readingMode);
    }
    // Pre-apply spinout-banner dismissal here, before the banner paints, so it
    // never flashes in only to be hidden later by the deferred arxiv-header.js.
    // Key matches arxiv-header.js: "arxiv-banner-dismissed:" + data-banner-name.
    if (localStorage.getItem('arxiv-banner-dismissed:spinout-nonprofit')) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-banner-dismissed", "");
    }
  }
  // Run as soon as JS starts, to minimize repainting
  initializeReadingPreferences();
</script>

<li class="ltx_tocentry ltx_tocentry_subsection"><a href="#S4.SS5" title="In 4 Experimental Results ‣ DeepSeek-Coder-V2: Breaking the Barrier of Closed-Source Models in Code Intelligence" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_title"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_ref">4.5 </span>Mathematical Reasoning</span></a></li>
<li class="ltx_tocentry ltx_tocentry_subsection"><a href="#S4.SS6" title="In 4 Experimental Results ‣ DeepSeek-Coder-V2: Breaking the Barrier of Closed-Source Models in Code Intelligence" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_title"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_ref">4.6 </span>General Natural Language</span></a></li>
</ol></li>
<li class="ltx_tocentry ltx_tocentry_section"><a href="#S5" title="In DeepSeek-Coder-V2: Breaking the Barrier of Closed-Source Models in Code Intelligence" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_title"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_ref">5 </span>Conclusion</span></a></li>

<h1 class="ltx_title ltx_title_document">DeepSeek-Coder-V2: Breaking the Barrier of Closed-Source Models in Code Intelligence
</h1>
<div class="ltx_authors">
<span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname"><span id="id1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Qihao Zhu*, Daya Guo*, Zhihong Shao*, Dejian Yang*, Peiyi Wang, Runxin Xu, Y. Wu
<br class="ltx_break">Yukun Li, Huazuo Gao, Shirong Ma, Wangding Zeng, Xiao Bi, Zihui Gu, Hanwei Xu, Damai Dai
<br class="ltx_break">Kai Dong, Liyue Zhang, Yishi Piao, Zhibin Gou, Zhenda Xie, Zhewen Hao, Bingxuan Wang
<br class="ltx_break">Junxiao Song, Deli Chen, Xin Xie, Kang Guan, Yuxiang You, Aixin Liu, Qiushi Du, Wenjun Gao 
<br class="ltx_break">Xuan Lu, Qinyu Chen, Yaohui Wang, Chengqi Deng, Jiashi Li, Chenggang Zhao 
<br class="ltx_break">Chong Ruan, Fuli Luo, Wenfeng Liang
DeepSeek-AI 
<br class="ltx_break"><a href="https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-Coder-V2" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_url ltx_font_typewriter">https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-Coder-V2</a>

</span>
</span><span class="ltx_author_notes"><span class="ltx_author_notes_content">
<span class="ltx_contact ltx_role_correspondent"><span class="ltx_contact_name">Corresponding author: </span>Core contributors

</span></span></span></span></div>

<div id="abstract1" class="ltx_abstract"><h6 class="ltx_title ltx_title_abstract">Abstract</h6>
    
<p id="abstract1.1" class="ltx_p">We present DeepSeek-Coder-V2, an open-source Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) code language model that achieves performance comparable to GPT4-Turbo in code-specific tasks. Specifically, DeepSeek-Coder-V2 is further pre-trained from an intermediate checkpoint of DeepSeek-V2 with additional 6 trillion tokens. Through this continued pre-training, DeepSeek-Coder-V2 substantially enhances the coding and mathematical reasoning capabilities of DeepSeek-V2, while maintaining comparable performance in general language tasks. Compared to DeepSeek-Coder-33B, DeepSeek-Coder-V2 demonstrates significant advancements in various aspects of code-related tasks, as well as reasoning and general capabilities. Additionally, DeepSeek-Coder-V2 expands its support for programming languages from 86 to 338, while extending the context length from 16K to 128K.
In standard benchmark evaluations, DeepSeek-Coder-V2 achieves superior performance compared to closed-source models such as GPT4-Turbo, Claude 3 Opus, and Gemini 1.5 Pro in coding and math benchmarks.</p>
  
</div>
<figure id="S0.F1" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2406.11931v1/performance.svg" id="S0.F1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:438/213;" width="438" height="213"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 1: </span>The Performance of DeepSeek-Coder-V2 on math and code benchmarks.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
<section id="S1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">1 </span>Introduction</h2>

<div id="S1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The open-source community has made significant strides in advancing code intelligence through the development of open-source code models such as StarCoder <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2023b</a>; <a href="#bib.bib28" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lozhkov et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, CodeLlama <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib36" title="" class="ltx_ref">Roziere et al., 2023</a>)</cite>, DeepSeek-Coder <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Guo et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, and Codestral <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib31" title="" class="ltx_ref">MistralAI, 2024</a>)</cite>. These models have steadily approached the performance levels of closed-source counterparts, contributing to the progress of code intelligence. However, there remains a discernible gap when comparing them to state-of-the-art closed-source models like GPT4-Turbo <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib33" title="" class="ltx_ref">OpenAI, 2023</a>)</cite>, Claude 3 Opus <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">Anthropic, 2024</a>)</cite>, and Gemini 1.5 Pro <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib35" title="" class="ltx_ref">Reid et al., 2024</a>)</cite>. To bridge this gap and further propel the development of open-source code models, we introduce the DeepSeek-Coder-V2 series. These models are built upon the foundation of DeepSeek-V2 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">DeepSeek-AI, 2024</a>)</cite> and are further pre-trained with an additional corpus with 6 trillion tokens.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">In the pre-training phase, the dataset of DeepSeek-Coder-V2 is created with a composition of 60% source code, 10% math corpus, and 30% natural language corpus. The source code consists of 1,170B code-related tokens sourced from GitHub and CommonCrawl, using the same pipeline as DeepSeekMath <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib37" title="" class="ltx_ref">Shao et al., 2024</a>)</cite>. This corpus expands from 86 to 338 programming languages compared to the code corpus used to train DeepSeek-Coder. To demonstrate the effectiveness of the new code corpus, we conduct ablation studies with the 1B parameter model and observe improvements of 6.7% and 9.4% in accuracy across both HumanEval (from 30.5% to 37.2%) and MBPP (from 44.6% to 54.0%) benchmarks  <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al., 2021</a>; <a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">Austin et al., 2021a</a>)</cite>, respectively. For the math corpus, we collect 221B math-related tokens sourced from CommonCrawl using the same pipeline, which approximately doubles the size of the 120B DeepSeekMath corpus <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib37" title="" class="ltx_ref">Shao et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, while for the natural language corpus, we directly sample from the training corpus in DeepSeek-V2. In total, DeepSeek-Coder-V2 has been exposed to 10.2T training tokens, where 4.2 trillion tokens originate from the DeepSeek V2 dataset, while the remaining 6 trillion tokens come from the DeepSeek-Coder-V2 dataset.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">To accommodate longer code inputs and enhance applicability across various programming scenarios, we extend the context length from 16K to 128K tokens, allowing our models to handle more complex and extensive coding tasks. After continuous pre-training DeepSeek-V2 on this multi-source corpora, we find that DeepSeek-Coder-V2 significantly enhances the model’s capabilities in coding and mathematical reasoning while maintaining comparable general language performance.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">In the alignment phase, we first construct an instruction training dataset that includes code and math data from DeepSeek-Coder <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Guo et al., 2024</a>)</cite> and DeepSeek-Math <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib37" title="" class="ltx_ref">Shao et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, as well as general instruction data from DeepSeek-V2 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">DeepSeek-AI, 2024</a>)</cite>. This dataset is used to fine-tune the base model. Then, in the reinforcement learning phase, we employ Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) algorithm to align its behavior with human preferences. Preference data is collected in the coding domain using compiler feedback and test cases, and a reward model is developed to guide the training of the policy model. This approach ensures that the model’s responses are optimized for correctness and human preference in coding tasks. To enable the model to support code completion after alignment, we also utilize Fill-In-Middle approach <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Guo et al., 2024</a>)</cite> during the fine-tuning of the base model with 16B parameters.</p>
</div>
<section id="S1.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">1.1 </span>Contributions</h3>

<div id="S1.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In summary, our main contributions are:</p>
<ul id="S1.I1" class="ltx_itemize" style="--ltx-enum-leftmargin:20pt;">
<li id="S1.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We introduce DeepSeek-Coder-V2 with 16B and 236B parameters based on the DeepSeekMoE framework, which has activation parameters of only 2.4B and 21B, efficiently supporting diverse computational and application needs. Additionally, DeepSeek-Coder-V2 supports 338 programming languages and a maximum context length of 128K tokens.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We make the first attempt to develop an open-source hundred-billion-parameter code model to advance the field of code intelligence. Experimental results indicate that DeepSeek-Coder-V2 236B outperforms state-of-the-art closed-source models, such as GPT4-Turbo, Claude 3 Opus, and Gemini 1.5 Pro, in both coding and mathematics tasks.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">DeepSeek-Coder-V2 models are released publicly under a permissive license, allowing for both research and unrestricted commercial use.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S1.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">1.2 </span>Summary of Evaluations and Metrics</h3>

<div id="S1.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<ul id="S1.I2" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S1.I2.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I2.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I2.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.I2.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Code</span>: Regarding code generation benchmark evaluation, DeepSeek-Coder-V2 demonstrates remarkable superiority over all open source models while exhibiting performance on par with the leading closed-source models, such as GPT4-Turbo, Claude 3 Opus, and Gemini 1.5 Pro. Notably, we achieve a <span id="S1.I2.i1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">90.2</span>% score on HumanEval <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al., 2021</a>)</cite>, a <span id="S1.I2.i1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">76.2</span>% score on MBPP <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">Austin et al., 2021a</a>)</cite> (establishing a new state-of-the-art result with EvalPlus evaluation pipeline), and a <span id="S1.I2.i1.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">43.4</span>% score on LiveCodeBench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Jain et al., 2024</a>)</cite> (questions from Dec. 2023 to June. 2024). Additionally, DeepSeek-Coder-V2 is the first open-source model that surpasses a score of 10% on SWEBench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">Jimenez et al., 2023</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I2.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I2.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I2.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.I2.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Math</span>:
DeepSeek-Coder-V2 exhibits strong mathematical reasoning abilities, rivaling top closed-source models such as GPT-4o, Gemini 1.5 Pro, and Claude 3 Opus on both elementary benchmarks like GSM8K <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Cobbe et al., 2021</a>)</cite> and advanced competition-level benchmarks including MATH <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">Hendrycks et al., 2021</a>)</cite>, AIME <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">MAA, 2024</a>)</cite>, and Math Odyssey <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib32" title="" class="ltx_ref">Netmind.AI, 2024</a>)</cite>.
Notably, DeepSeek-Coder-V2 attains an accuracy of <span id="S1.I2.i2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">75.7</span>% on the MATH benchmark, nearly matching the state-of-the-art accuracy of <span id="S1.I2.i2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">76.6</span>% achieved by GPT-4o.
Furthermore, it surpasses the performance of these closed-source models in the AIME 2024 competition.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I2.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I2.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I2.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.I2.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Natural Language</span>: DeepSeek-Coder-V2 maintains comparable general language performance to DeepSeek-V2. For example, DeepSeek-Coder-V2 achieves 79.2% on MMLU with OpenAI simple-eval pipeline. Regarding subjective evaluation with GPT-4 as a judger, DeepSeek-Coder-V2 achieves <span id="S1.I2.i3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">65.0</span> on arena-hard <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, <span id="S1.I2.i3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">8.77</span> on MT-bench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib42" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zheng et al., 2023</a>)</cite> and <span id="S1.I2.i3.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">7.84</span> on alignbench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2023c</a>)</cite>. These scores are significantly better than other code-specific models, even comparable with general open source models.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S2" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">2 </span>Data Collection</h2>

<div id="S2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The pre-training data for DeepSeek-Coder-V2 primarily consists of 60% source code, 10% math corpus, and 30% natural language corpus. Since the natural language corpus is directly sampled from the training dataset of DeepSeek-V2, this section focuses on the collection, cleaning, and filtering processes of the code and math data. Meanwhile, we further validate the quality of this data through comparative analysis experiments.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We collect public repositories created before November 2023 on GitHub. We first apply the same filtering rules and near-deduplication as those used in the DeepSeek-Coder <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Guo et al., 2024</a>)</cite> to filter out lower-quality and duplicated source code. To make the paper self-contained, we briefly describe the filtering rules. Firstly, we filter out files with an average line length exceeding 100 characters or a maximum line length surpassing 1000 characters. Additionally, we remove files with fewer than 25% alphabetic characters. Except for the XSLT programming language, we further filter out files where the string <span id="S2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">"&lt;?xml version="</span> appears in the first 100 characters. For HTML files, we consider the ratio of visible text to HTML code. We retain files where the visible text constitutes at least 20% of the code and is no less than 100 characters. For JSON and YAML files, which typically contain more data, we only keep files that have a character count ranging from 50 to 5000 characters. This effectively removes most data-heavy files. By applying these filtering rules and near-deduplication, we obtain 821B code encompassing 338 programming languages and 185B code-related text, such as markdown and issues. The list of supported programming languages can be found in the Appendix <a href="#A1" title="Appendix A Supported Programming Languages ‣ DeepSeek-Coder-V2: Breaking the Barrier of Closed-Source Models in Code Intelligence" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A</span></a>. We use the same tokenizer as DeepSeekV2, detailed in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">DeepSeek-AI, 2024</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">To collect code-related and math-related web texts from Common Crawl, we follow the same pipeline as DeepSeekMath <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib37" title="" class="ltx_ref">Shao et al., 2024</a>)</cite>. Specifically, we select coding forums such as StackOverflow<span id="footnote1" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">1</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">1</sup>
            <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">1</span>
            
            
            
          https://stackoverflow.com</span></span></span>, library sites such as PyTorch documentation<span id="footnote2" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">2</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">2</sup>
            <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">2</span>
            
            
            
          https://pytorch.org/docs</span></span></span>, and mathematics website such as StackExchange<span id="footnote3" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">3</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">3</sup>
            <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">3</span>
            
            
            
          https://math.stackexchange.com</span></span></span>
as our initial seed corpus. Using this seed corpus, we train a fastText model <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">Joulin et al., 2016</a>)</cite> to recall more coding-related and math-related web pages. Since tokenization for languages like Chinese cannot be done through spaces, we use the Byte Pair Encoding (BPE) tokenizer from DeepSeek-V2, which significantly improves the recall accuracy of fastText. For each domain, we calculate the percentage of web pages collected in the first iteration. Domains with over 10% of web pages collected are classified as code-related or math-related. We then annotate the URLs associated with code-related or math-related content within these identified domains. Uncollected web pages linked to these URLs are added to the seed corpus. After three iterations of data collection, we gather 70 billion code-related tokens and 221B math-related tokens from web pages.
To further collect high-quality source code from GitHub, we also apply the same pipeline on GitHub with two iterations of data collection and collect 94B source code. The initial seed corpus is constructed by manually collecting high-quality source code, such as those containing detailed descriptions. Finally, the new code corpus consists of 1,170B code-related tokens sourced from GitHub and CommonCrawl.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.p4.1" class="ltx_p">To demonstrate the effectiveness of the new code corpus, we conducted ablation studies (see Table <a href="#S2.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ 2 Data Collection ‣ DeepSeek-Coder-V2: Breaking the Barrier of Closed-Source Models in Code Intelligence" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>) using a 1B parameter model, comparing it with the corpus used to train DeepSeek-Coder. Pre-training the 1B model on the new code corpus using 1T tokens resulted in improvements of 5.5% and 4.4% in accuracy on the HumanEval (from 30.5% to 36.0%) and MBPP (from 44.6% to 49.0%) benchmarks, respectively. Further training the 1B model with 2T tokens led to additional improvements, with HumanEval and MBPP scores rising to 37.2% and 54.0%, respectively. Therefore, the new code corpus is superior to the code corpus used to train DeepSeek-Coder.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S2.T1" class="ltx_table">

</section>
<section id="S3" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">3 </span>Training Policy</h2>

<section id="S3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.1 </span>Training Strategy</h3>

<div id="S3.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We use two training objectives for DeepSeek-Coder-v2 16B: Next-Token-Prediction and Fill-In-Middle (FIM)  <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2023b</a>; <a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Bavarian et al., 2022</a>; <a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Guo et al., 2024</a>)</cite>. For DeepSeek-Coder-v2 236B, we only utilize the Next-Token-Prediction objective.
Here we give a brief introduction of the FIM training policy. We adopt the FIM training approach for the development of DeepSeek-Coder-v2-16B, leveraging the PSM (Prefix, Suffix, Middle) mode. This method structures the content reconstruction in the sequence: Prefix, Suffix, and Middle, as illustrated below:</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<table id="S3.EGx1" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S3.Ex1"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.Ex1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\texttt{&lt;｜fim\_begin｜&gt;}f_{pre}\texttt{&lt;｜fim\_hole｜&gt;}f_{suf}\texttt{&lt;｜fim\_end｜&gt;}f_{middle}\texttt{&lt;|eos\_token|&gt;}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">&lt;｜fim_begin｜&gt;</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">&lt;｜fim_hole｜&gt;</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>u</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>f</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">&lt;｜fim_end｜&gt;</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>l</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">&lt;|eos_token|&gt;</mtext></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\texttt{&lt;｜fim\_begin｜&gt;}f_{pre}\texttt{&lt;｜fim\_hole｜&gt;}f_{suf}\texttt{&lt;｜fim\_end｜&gt;}f_{middle}\texttt{&lt;|eos\_token|&gt;}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">This structure is applied at the document level as part of the pre-packing process. The FIM is utilized at a rate of 0.5, consistent with the PSM framework, to enhance the training efficacy and model performance.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.2 </span>Model Architecture</h3>

<div id="S3.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Our architecture aligns with that of DeepSeekV2 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">DeepSeek-AI, 2024</a>)</cite>. The hyperparameters settings, 16B and 236B, correspond to those used in DeepSeek-V2-Lite and DeepSeek-V2, respectively. Notably, we encountered instability during training and spikes in gradient values, which we attributed to the exponential normalization technique. To address this, we reverted to the conventional normalization method.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.3 </span>Training Hyper-Parameters</h3>

<div id="S3.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Consistent with the DeepSeek V2 methodology <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">DeepSeek-AI, 2024</a>)</cite>, we utilize the AdamW optimizer <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">Loshchilov and Hutter, 2019</a>)</cite>, configured with <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta_{1}=0.9" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta_{1}=0.9</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta_{2}=0.95" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.95</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta_{2}=0.95</annotation></semantics></math>, and a weight decay of 0.1. Batch sizes and learning rates are adjusted according to DeepSeek-V2 specifications. For learning rate scheduling, we employ a cosine decay strategy, starting with 2000 warm-up steps and gradually reducing the learning rate to 10% of its initial value.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Both DeepSeek-Coder-V2 and DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite are trained using the same methodology. To maintain robust natural language understanding capabilities in DeepSeek-Coder-V2, we continue the pre-training process from an intermediate checkpoint of DeepSeek-V2. The intermediate checkpoint was initially trained on 4.2T tokens. Consequently, DeepSeek-Coder-V2 has been exposed to a total of 10.2T high-quality tokens during the pre-training phase.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S3.T2" class="ltx_table">
<table id="S3.T2.2" class="ltx_tabular ltx_guessed_headers ltx_align_middle">
<thead class="ltx_thead">
<tr id="S3.T2.2.1" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="S3.T2.2.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_th_row ltx_border_r ltx_border_tt"><span id="S3.T2.2.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Model</span></th>
<th id="S3.T2.2.1.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_r ltx_border_tt"><span id="S3.T2.2.1.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite</span></th>
<th id="S3.T2.2.1.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt"><span id="S3.T2.2.1.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">DeepSeek-Coder-V2</span></th></tr>
</thead>
<tbody class="ltx_tbody">
<tr id="S3.T2.2.2" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="S3.T2.2.2.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_row ltx_border_r ltx_border_t"><span id="S3.T2.2.2.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;"># Total Parameters (#TP)</span></th>
<td id="S3.T2.2.2.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_r ltx_border_t"><span id="S3.T2.2.2.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">16B</span></td>
<td id="S3.T2.2.2.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_t"><span id="S3.T2.2.2.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">236B</span></td></tr>
<tr id="S3.T2.2.3" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="S3.T2.2.3.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_row ltx_border_r ltx_border_t"><span id="S3.T2.2.3.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;"># Active Parameters (#AP)</span></th>
<td id="S3.T2.2.3.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_r ltx_border_t"><span id="S3.T2.2.3.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">2.4B</span></td>
<td id="S3.T2.2.3.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_t"><span id="S3.T2.2.3.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">21B</span></td></tr>
<tr id="S3.T2.2.4" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="S3.T2.2.4.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_row ltx_border_r ltx_border_t"><span id="S3.T2.2.4.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Pre-training Tokens</span></th>
<td id="S3.T2.2.4.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_r ltx_border_t"><span id="S3.T2.2.4.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">4.2T+6T</span></td>
<td id="S3.T2.2.4.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_t"><span id="S3.T2.2.4.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">4.2T+6T</span></td></tr>
<tr id="S3.T2.2.5" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="S3.T2.2.5.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_row ltx_border_r ltx_border_t"><span id="S3.T2.2.5.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">LR Scheduler</span></th>
<td id="S3.T2.2.5.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_r ltx_border_t"><span id="S3.T2.2.5.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Cosine</span></td>
<td id="S3.T2.2.5.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_t"><span id="S3.T2.2.5.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Cosine</span></td></tr>
<tr id="S3.T2.2.6" class="ltx_tr">

<td id="S3.T2.2.6.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb ltx_border_r ltx_border_t"><span id="S3.T2.2.6.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Enable</span></td>
<td id="S3.T2.2.6.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb ltx_border_t"><span id="S3.T2.2.6.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Disable</span></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 2: </span>Training Setting of DeepSeek-Coder-V2. </figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.4 </span>Long Context Extension</h3>

<div id="S3.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Following DeepSeek-V2, we extend the context length of DeepSeek-Coder-V2 to 128K using Yarn <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib34" title="" class="ltx_ref">Peng et al., 2023</a>)</cite>. The hyper-parameters of YARN are the same as DeepSeek-V2: the scale <math id="S3.SS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math> to 40, <math id="S3.SS4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>α</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha</annotation></semantics></math> to 1, <math id="S3.SS4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>β</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta</annotation></semantics></math> to 32.
We further continue training the model using two stages to enhance its capability for handling long contexts. In the first stage, we utilize a sequence length of 32K and a batch size of 1152 for 1000 steps. In the second stage, we train the model for an additional 1000 steps, employing a sequence length of 128K and a batch size of 288 sequences. It should be noted here we upsample long context data ratio during long context extension. As shown in Figure <a href="#S3.F2" title="Figure 2 ‣ 3.4 Long Context Extension ‣ 3 Training Policy ‣ DeepSeek-Coder-V2: Breaking the Barrier of Closed-Source Models in Code Intelligence" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>, the results on the “Needle In A Haystack” (NIAH) tests indicate that DeepSeek-Coder-V2 performs well across all context window lengths up to 128K.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S3.F2" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2406.11931v1/longcontext.png" id="S3.F2.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:390/205;" width="390" height="205" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 2: </span>
Evaluation results on the “Needle In A Haystack” (NIAH) tests. DeepSeek-Coder-V2 performs well across all context window lengths up to 128K.
</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.5 </span>Alignment</h3>

<section id="S3.SS5.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">3.5.1 </span>Supervised Fine-Tuning</h4>

<div id="S3.SS5.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS5.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To build DeepSeek-Coder-V2 Chat, we construct the instruction training dataset mixed with code and math data. We first collect 20k code-related instruction data and 30k math related data from DeepSeek-Coder and DeepSeek-Math. To maintain the general ability, we also sample several data from the instruction data of DeepSeek-V2. Finally, we use a instruction dataset of 300M tokens. For training, we use a cosine schedule with 100 warm-up steps and an initial learning rate <math id="S3.SS5.SSS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5e^{-6}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5e^{-6}</annotation></semantics></math>. We also use a batch size of 1M tokens and 1B tokens in total.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS5.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">3.5.2 </span>Reinforcement Learning</h4>

<div id="S3.SS5.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS5.SSS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We further employ Reinforcement Learning (RL) techniques to fully simulate the capabilities of DeepSeek-Coder-V2, which is proven to be quite effective.</p>
</div>
<section id="S3.SS5.SSS2.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Prompts</h5>

<div id="S3.SS5.SSS2.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS5.SSS2.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Considerable effort was spent collecting prompts related to code and math from various sources, and each code prompt comes with corresponding test cases.
After filtering the prompts, there are approximately 40k data in total.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS5.SSS2.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Reward Modeling</h5>

<div id="S3.SS5.SSS2.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS5.SSS2.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Reward models play crucial roles in the RL training.
In terms of mathematical preference data, we obtain them using the ground-truth labels.
In terms of code preference data, although the code compiler itself can already provide 0-1 feedback (whether the code pass all test cases or not), some code prompts may have a limited number of test cases, and do not provide full coverage, and hence directly using 0-1 feedback from the compiler may be noisy and sub-optimal.
Therefore, we still decide to train a reward model on the data provided by the compiler, and use the reward model to provide signal during RL training, which is more robust and has better generalization ability, in comparison with raw compiler signal.
As illustrated in Figure <a href="#S3.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ Reinforcement Learning Algorithm ‣ 3.5.2 Reinforcement Learning ‣ 3.5 Alignment ‣ 3 Training Policy ‣ DeepSeek-Coder-V2: Breaking the Barrier of Closed-Source Models in Code Intelligence" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>, in our in-house test sets (Leetcode and Leetcode-zh), using a reward model to provide RL training signal clearly outperforms using raw compiler signal.
Hence, we use reward model signal rather than compiler signal in all subsequent experiments.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS5.SSS2.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Reinforcement Learning Algorithm</h5>

<div id="S3.SS5.SSS2.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS5.SSS2.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We employ Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib37" title="" class="ltx_ref">Shao et al. (2024)</a></cite> as our RL algorithm, which is the same as what DeepSeek-V2 uses.
Notably, GRPO is proven to be quite effective and has less cost compared with PPO, since there is no need to maintain an additional critic model.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S3.F3" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2406.11931v1/rl.svg" id="S3.F3.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:438/146;" width="438" height="146"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 3: </span>Performances of Different Methods</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">4 </span>Experimental Results</h2>

<div id="S4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this section, we evaluate DeepSeek-Coder-V2 on three types of tasks, including coding, mathematics, and general natural language. We compare DeepSeek-Coder-V2 with the previous state-of-the-art large language models.</p>
<ul id="S4.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S4.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S4.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">CodeLlama</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib36" title="" class="ltx_ref">Roziere et al., 2023</a>)</cite> consists of a series of code language models based on Llama2 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib40" title="" class="ltx_ref">Touvron et al., 2023</a>)</cite>, and continue pre-training on datasets ranging from 500 to 1000 billion code tokens. These models are available in four sizes: 7B, 13B, 34B, and 70B.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S4.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S4.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">StarCoder</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib28" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lozhkov et al., 2024</a>)</cite> is a publicly accessible model with 15 billion parameters. It is specifically trained on a meticulously curated subset of the Stack dataset <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kocetkov et al., 2022</a>)</cite>, covering 86 programming languages.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S4.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S4.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">StarCoder2</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib28" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lozhkov et al., 2024</a>)</cite> consists of 3B, 7B, and 15B parameters models trained on 3.3 to 4.3 trillion tokens of the Stack2 dataset <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib28" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lozhkov et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, spanning 619 programming languages.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S4.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S4.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.I1.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">DeepSeek-Coder</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Guo et al., 2024</a>)</cite> comprises a series of code language models, ranging from 1 billion to 33 billion parameters. Each model is trained from scratch on 2 trillion tokens, with a composition of 87% code and 13% natural language in both English and Chinese. These models are pre-trained on a project-level code corpus using a window size of 16K and an additional fill-in-the-blank task, enabling support for project-level code completion and infilling.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S4.I1.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S4.I1.i5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I1.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.I1.i5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Codestral</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib31" title="" class="ltx_ref">MistralAI, 2024</a>)</cite> is a 22B parameter model developed by Mistral. It is trained on a diverse dataset of over 80 programming languages, including popular ones such as Python, Java, and JavaScript, as well as more specialized languages like Swift and Fortran.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S4.I1.i6" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S4.I1.i6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I1.i6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">General language models that we compare include <span id="S4.I1.i6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Llama3 70B</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib30" title="" class="ltx_ref">Meta, 2024</a>)</cite>, <span id="S4.I1.i6.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">GPT-4</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib33" title="" class="ltx_ref">OpenAI, 2023</a>)</cite>, <span id="S4.I1.i6.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Claude 3 Opus</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">Anthropic, 2024</a>)</cite>, and <span id="S4.I1.i6.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Gemini 1.5 Pro</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib35" title="" class="ltx_ref">Reid et al., 2024</a>)</cite>. While they are not specifically trained on large code corpora, they achieve state-of-the-art performance in coding.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.1 </span>Code Generation</h3>

<section id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">HumanEval and MBPP Benchmarks.</h5>

<div id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The HumanEval <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al., 2021</a>)</cite> <span id="footnote4" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">4</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">4</sup>
                <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">4</span>
                
                
                
              We use the template ”Please complete the python function below. The final complete version of your function must be returned within a code block. Here is the unfinished function:\n ```python\n{problem_description}\n\n” to build the instruction prompt.</span></span></span> and MBPP <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">Austin et al., 2021b</a>)</cite> benchmarks are commonly utilized for assessing the performance of code-generating Large Language Models (LLMs). HumanEval comprises 164 Python tasks that are verified through test cases to evaluate the performance of Code LLMs in a zero-shot scenario. For MBPP, we use the MBPP-Plus version <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2023a</a>)</cite> to evaluate the models. To test the multilingual abilities of models, we extended the HumanEval benchmark problems into seven additional languages: C++, Java, PHP, TypeScript, C#, Bash, JavaScript, Swift, R, Julia, D, Rust and Racket. For both benchmarks, we employed a greedy search strategy and recreated the baseline results using identical scripts and environments to ensure a fair comparison.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.T3" class="ltx_table">
<div id="S4.T3.2" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_transformed_outer" style="width:345.0pt;height:210.2pt;vertical-align:-103.6pt;"><span class="ltx_transformed_inner" style="transform:translate(-87.9pt,53.5pt) scale(0.7,0.7) ;">
<p id="S4.T3.2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.T3.2.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">

<span id="S4.T3.2.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.T3.2.1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text">

<span id="S4.T3.2.1.1.1.1.1.1.3" class="ltx_tr">
<span id="S4.T3.2.1.1.1.1.1.1.3.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_th_row ltx_border_t">Gemini-1.5-Pro</span>
<span id="S4.T3.2.1.1.1.1.1.1.3.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_t">-</span>

<span id="S4.T3.2.1.1.1.1.1.1.3.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_t">81.0%</span>

<span id="S4.T3.2.1.1.1.1.1.1.3.7" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_t">75.3%</span>
<span id="S4.T3.2.1.1.1.1.1.1.3.8" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_t">77.4%</span>
<span id="S4.T3.2.1.1.1.1.1.1.3.9" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_t">80.8%</span>
<span id="S4.T3.2.1.1.1.1.1.1.3.10" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_t">74.5%</span>
<span id="S4.T3.2.1.1.1.1.1.1.3.11" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_t">39.9%</span></span>

<figcaption class="ltx_caption" style="font-size:90%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 3: </span>Performance Metrics for Various Models on HumanEval and MBPP Benchmarks</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#S4.T3" title="Table 3 ‣ HumanEval and MBPP Benchmarks. ‣ 4.1 Code Generation ‣ 4 Experimental Results ‣ DeepSeek-Coder-V2: Breaking the Barrier of Closed-Source Models in Code Intelligence" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> provides an extensive overview of the performance metrics for various models across multiple programming languages on the HumanEval and <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{MBPP}^{+}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mtext>MBPP</mtext><mo>+</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{MBPP}^{+}</annotation></semantics></math> Benchmarks. The DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Instruct demonstrates exceptional performance, securing the second-highest average score of 75.3%. This performance is notable as it breaks the dominance typically seen from closed-source models, standing out as a leading open-source contender. It is surpassed only by GPT-4o, which leads with an average score of 76.4%. DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Instruct shows top-tier results across a variety of languages, including the highest scores in Java and PHP, and strong performances in Python, C++, C#, TypeScript, and JavaScript, underscoring its robustness and versatility in handling diverse coding challenges.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Furthermore, the DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite-Instruct also performs impressively, surpassing the larger 33B model. With a considerable margin in average performance (65.6% vs. 61.9%), it highlights the effectiveness of the 16B model in delivering competitive results despite its smaller size. This underscores the model’s efficiency and the advancements in model architecture and training methodologies that allow it to outperform larger counterparts.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Competitive Programming.</h5>

<div id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To further validate the model’s capability in real-world competitive programming problems, we utilize the LiveCodeBench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Jain et al., 2024</a>)</cite> and USACO benchmark <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib38" title="" class="ltx_ref">Shi et al., 2024</a>)</cite> to estimate the effectiveness of DeepSeek-Coder-V2. LiveCodeBench is a meticulous and contamination-free assessment of Large Language Models (LLMs) for code generation, systematically gathering novel challenges over time from three prominent competitive programming platforms: LeetCode, AtCoder, and CodeForces. Since the cut-off of the training data is before November 2023, we use the subset (1201-0601) of Livecodebench. USACO benchmark contains 307 problems from the USA Computing
Olympiad, along with high-quality unit tests, reference code, and official
analyses for each problem.</p>
</div>

<td id="S4.T4.2.1.14.6" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb"><span id="S4.T4.2.1.14.6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">5.3%</span></td>

<td id="S4.T4.2.1.14.8" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb"><span id="S4.T4.2.1.14.8.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">12.1%</span></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</span></div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption" style="font-size:90%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 4: </span>Performance on the LiveCodeBench (LCB) and USACO benchmarks.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#S4.T4" title="Table 4 ‣ Competitive Programming. ‣ 4.1 Code Generation ‣ 4 Experimental Results ‣ DeepSeek-Coder-V2: Breaking the Barrier of Closed-Source Models in Code Intelligence" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> showcases the performance of various language models on the two benchmarks. Notably, DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Instruct delivers a standout performance, tying for the highest score among large models at 43.4%, on par with GPT-4o. This exceptional result places it second overall, just behind GPT-4-Turbo-0409, which leads with an overall performance of 45.7%. DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Instruct’s impressive ability to handle complex coding challenges firmly establishes it as a top contender, closely trailing the leading GPT-4-Turbo variant.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.2 </span>Code Completion</h3>

<section id="S4.SS2.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">4.2.1 </span>Repository-Level Code Completion Evaluation</h4>

<div id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We use RepoBench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2023b</a>)</cite> to evaluate the capabilities of currently available open-source code models with sizes below 35B in repository-level code completion tasks. This dataset is constructed from a diverse set of real-world, open-sourced, permissively licensed repositories in two popular programming languages: Python and Java. Notably, the latest version (v1.1) of RepoBench sources its data from GitHub repositories created between October 6th and December 31st, 2023, while our pre-training data includes code created before November 2023. To ensure this dataset was not present in our pre-training data and avoid data leakage, we only use data from December 2023.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Our evaluation includes five context length levels—2k, 4k, 8k, 12k, and 16k tokens—across three settings: cross-file-first, cross-file-random, and in-file. We use greedy search for all models under evaluation. The models were constrained to generate a maximum of 64 new tokens per prompt, and the first non-empty and non-comment line of the output was selected as the prediction. The maximum token length for prompts was set to 15,800 by truncating excess cross-file context. We report the average exact match for the different context length levels.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.T5" class="ltx_table">
<div id="S4.T5.2" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_transformed_outer" style="width:345.0pt;height:64.6pt;vertical-align:-31.1pt;"><span class="ltx_transformed_inner" style="transform:translate(-152.9pt,28.7pt) scale(0.530075080090619,0.530075080090619) ;">

</span></div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption" style="font-size:90%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 5: </span>Performance of different models on December subset of RepoBench v1.1.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">As shown in Table <a href="#S4.T5" title="Table 5 ‣ 4.2.1 Repository-Level Code Completion Evaluation ‣ 4.2 Code Completion ‣ 4 Experimental Results ‣ DeepSeek-Coder-V2: Breaking the Barrier of Closed-Source Models in Code Intelligence" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>, the results indicate that the DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite-Base model, despite having only 2.4 billion active parameters, achieves code completion capabilities in Python comparable to the DeepSeek-Coder-Base 33B model and in Java comparable to the DeepSeek-Coder-Base 7B model. Compared to CodeStral, the DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite-Base model has only one-tenth of the active parameters of CodeStral, resulting in lower performance in code completion tasks. However, we believe that the smaller number of active parameters in DeepSeek-Coder-V2 makes it faster for code completion scenarios.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">4.2.2 </span>Fill-in-the-Middle Code Completion</h4>

<div id="S4.SS2.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite is trained with a unique approach that includes a 0.5 Fill-In-the-Middle (FIM) rate during their pre-training phase. This method allows the model to adeptly complete code by filling in blanks using the surrounding context, which includes both the preceding and following code segments. This ability is particularly advantageous for code completion tools. Several open-source models, such as SantaCoder <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Allal et al., 2023</a>)</cite>, StarCoder <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2023b</a>)</cite>, and CodeLlama <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib36" title="" class="ltx_ref">Roziere et al., 2023</a>)</cite>, also leverage similar capabilities and have established high standards in the domain of code generation and completion.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.SSS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">To evaluate the performance of DeepSeek-Coder-V2 models, we conducted a comparative analysis against leading models. The assessment was based on the Single-Line Infilling benchmarks, covering three different programming languages as described by <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Allal et al. (2023)</a></cite>. The main metric for this evaluation was the line exact match accuracy<span id="footnote5" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">5</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">5</sup>
                <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">5</span>
                
                
                
              We use the first generated line rather than the whole generated chunk, thus the result is slightly different with DeepSeek-Coder.</span></span></span>.</p>
</div>

<figcaption class="ltx_caption" style="font-size:90%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 6: </span>Performance of different approaches on the FIM-Tasks.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S4.SS2.SSS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The table presents the performance of various coding models on FIM (Fill-in-the-Middle) tasks across three programming languages: Python, Java, and JavaScript, with a Mean score indicating overall effectiveness. Among the compared models, DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite-Base, with a configuration of 2.4B active parameters, achieves outstanding results. It scores 80.0% in Python, 89.1% in Java, and 87.2% in JavaScript, leading to a top Mean score of 86.4%. This demonstrates the superior effectiveness of DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite-Base, particularly in handling FIM tasks across different programming languages, achieving comparable performance with other bigger models in the evaluation.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.3 </span>Code Fixing </h3>

<div id="S4.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To evaluate the bug-fixing capabilities of the model, we used the Defects4J <span id="footnote7" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">7</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">7</sup>
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">7</span>
              
              
              
            https://github.com/rjust/defects4j</span></span></span>, SWE-bench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">Jimenez et al., 2023</a>)</cite>, and Aider <span id="footnote8" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">8</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">8</sup>
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">8</span>
              
              
              
            https://github.com/paul-gauthier/aider</span></span></span> datasets for testing. Defects4J is a widely used dataset in the field of software engineering, specifically designed for the purpose of evaluating and testing program repair techniques. It consists of a collection of real-world software bugs from various open-source projects, including but not limited to Apache Commons, JFreeChart, and Closure Compiler. Each bug in the dataset is accompanied by test suites that can be used to validate the effectiveness of program repair tools. Since the original bugs in Defec4J may need modify several files in the repository resulting in a long context, we collect 238 bugs that only need to modify one method from this benchmark.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">SWE-bench is a comprehensive benchmark designed to evaluate the performance of large language models in addressing real-world software issues sourced from GitHub. The benchmark presents a codebase alongside a specific issue, challenging the language model to generate a patch that effectively resolves the described problem. This rigorous evaluation framework ensures that the language model’s ability to understand and fix real-world software issues is thoroughly tested, providing a clear measure of its practical utility and effectiveness in software development tasks.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Aider’s code editing benchmark evaluates the LLM’s ability to modify Python source files, completing 133 distinct coding tasks. This benchmark not only tests the LLM’s coding skills but also checks its consistency in producing code edits according to the specifications in the prompt. For DeepSeek-Coder-V2 models, we use <span id="S4.SS3.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">whole</span> format to evaluate.</p>
</div>

<figcaption class="ltx_caption" style="font-size:90%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 7: </span>Performances of different models on repair benchmarks. We do not evaluate Llama3-Instruct on SWE-Bench as it just supports 8K context length. </figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S4.SS3.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#S4.T7" title="Table 7 ‣ 4.3 Code Fixing ‣ 4 Experimental Results ‣ DeepSeek-Coder-V2: Breaking the Barrier of Closed-Source Models in Code Intelligence" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> outlines the performances of different language models on software repair benchmarks, including Defects4J, SWE-Bench, and Aider. Among open-source models, DeepSeek-Coder-Instruct emerges as a standout, achieving the best performance within the open source models. It scores 21% in Defects4J and 12.7% in SWE-Bench, closely approaching the results of leading closed-source models and demonstrating significant capability in handling longer code sequences. Notably, DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Instruct achieves the highest score of 73.7% in Aider, surpassing all other models listed, including closed-source counterparts. This superior performance highlights its efficiency and robustness in automated code repair tasks, positioning DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Instruct as the top open-source model and a formidable competitor to closed-source alternatives in the field.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.4 </span>Code Understanding and Reasoning </h3>

<div id="S4.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To assess the code reasoning capabilities of our models, we utilize the CRUXEval benchmark. This benchmark comprises 800 Python functions paired with corresponding input-output examples. It is divided into two distinct tasks: CRUXEval-I, which requires the large language model (LLM) to predict the output based on the given input, and CRUXEval-O, where the model must predict the input from the known output. This structure challenges the model’s ability to understand and reason through Python code in both forward and reverse directions.</p>
</div>

<td id="S4.T8.2.1.12.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_t"><span id="S4.T8.2.1.12.4.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">53.0%</span></td>
<td id="S4.T8.2.1.12.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_t"><span id="S4.T8.2.1.12.5.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">52.9%</span></td></tr>
<tr id="S4.T8.2.1.13" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="S4.T8.2.1.13.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_row ltx_border_bb"><span id="S4.T8.2.1.13.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">DS-Coder-V2-Instruct</span></th>
<td id="S4.T8.2.1.13.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb"><span id="S4.T8.2.1.13.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">236B</span></td>

<td id="S4.T8.2.1.13.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb"><span id="S4.T8.2.1.13.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">75.1%</span></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</span></div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption" style="font-size:90%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 8: </span>Performance of different models on the CruxEval benchmark.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S4.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#S4.T8" title="Table 8 ‣ 4.4 Code Understanding and Reasoning ‣ 4 Experimental Results ‣ DeepSeek-Coder-V2: Breaking the Barrier of Closed-Source Models in Code Intelligence" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a> presents the performance of various language models on the CruxEval benchmark, which assesses models on two metrics: CruxEval-I-COT and CruxEval-O-COT. Among the open-source models, DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Instruct stands out significantly. It scores 70.0% on CruxEval-I-COT and 75.1% on CruxEval-O-COT, showcasing its superior capability within the open-source domain. However, when compared to larger closed-source models, there is a performance gap. This performance gap may largely be attributed to the fact that DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Instruct operates with only 21 billion activation parameters, which is considerably fewer than those in larger, more advanced closed-source models like GPT-4o. This limitation in model complexity could restrict its learning and problem-solving capacities.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.5 </span>Mathematical Reasoning </h3>

<div id="S4.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To assess the mathematical reasoning capabilities of DeepSeekCoder-V2, we utilized the popular grade-school benchmark GSM8K <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Cobbe et al., 2021</a>)</cite>, along with advanced competition-level benchmarks including MATH <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">Hendrycks et al., 2021</a>)</cite>, the American Invitational Mathematics Examination (AIME) 2024 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">MAA, 2024</a>)</cite>, and Math Odyssey <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib32" title="" class="ltx_ref">Netmind.AI, 2024</a>)</cite><span id="footnote9" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">9</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">9</sup>
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">9</span>
              
              
              
            The performance of DeepSeek-Coder-V2 on the four mathematical benchmarks was obtained with zero-shot chain-of-thought prompting;
each test question was concatenated with the instruction: ”<math id="footnote9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\backslash" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>\</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\backslash</annotation></semantics></math>nPlease reason step by step, and put your final answer within <math id="footnote9.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\backslash" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>\</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\backslash</annotation></semantics></math>boxed{}.”</span></span></span>.</p>
</div>

<td id="S4.T9.2.11.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;"><span id="S4.T9.2.11.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">236B</span></td>
<td id="S4.T9.2.11.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;"><span id="S4.T9.2.11.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">21B</span></td>
<td id="S4.T9.2.11.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;"><span id="S4.T9.2.11.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">94.9%</span></td>
<td id="S4.T9.2.11.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;"><span id="S4.T9.2.11.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">75.7%</span></td>
<td id="S4.T9.2.11.6" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;"><span id="S4.T9.2.11.6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">4<span id="S4.T9.2.11.6.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">/</span>30</span></td>
<td id="S4.T9.2.11.7" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;"><span id="S4.T9.2.11.7.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">53.7%</span></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption" style="font-size:90%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 9: </span>
Performance of different models on the mathematical reasoning. DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Instruct can achieve 5/30 on AIME 2024 with maj@64.
</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S4.SS5.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The results, presented in Table <a href="#S4.T9" title="Table 9 ‣ 4.5 Mathematical Reasoning ‣ 4 Experimental Results ‣ DeepSeek-Coder-V2: Breaking the Barrier of Closed-Source Models in Code Intelligence" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>, were obtained using greedy decoding without the aid of tools or voting techniques, unless otherwise specified.
DeepSeek-Coder-V2 achieved an accuracy of 75.7% on the MATH benchmark and 53.7% on Math Odyssey, comparable to the state-of-the-art GPT-4o.
Additionally, DeepSeek-Coder-V2 solves more problems from AIME 2024 than the other models, demonstrating its strong mathematical reasoning capabilities.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS6" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.6 </span>General Natural Language </h3>

<div id="S4.SS6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">As DeepSeek-Coder-V2 is built upon DeepSeek-V2, it inherits the strong natural language capability, even surpassing DeepSeek-V2 on reasoning-related benchmarks. We compare DeepSeek-Coder-V2 Instruct with DeepSeek-V2 Chat on standard benchmarks, which covers both English and Chinese benchmarks, including BigBench Hard (BBH) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib39" title="" class="ltx_ref">Suzgun et al., 2022</a>)</cite>, MMLU <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">Hendrycks et al., 2020</a>)</cite>, ARC <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">Clark et al., 2018</a>)</cite>, TriviaQA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib17" title="" class="ltx_ref">Joshi et al., 2017</a>)</cite>, NaturalQuestions <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kwiatkowski et al., 2019</a>)</cite>, AGIEval <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhong et al., 2023</a>)</cite>， CLUEWSC <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib41" title="" class="ltx_ref">Xu et al., 2020</a>)</cite>, C-Eval <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Huang et al., 2023</a>)</cite>, and CMMLU <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2023a</a>)</cite>.
Besides, we also evaluate the open-ended generation ability of models, including Arena-Hard <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, AlpacaEval2.0 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">Dubois et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, MT-Bench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib42" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zheng et al., 2023</a>)</cite>, and Alignbench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2023c</a>)</cite>.
The evaluation pipeline and metrics are the same as in DeepSeek-V2, where the MMLU are evaluated using OpenAI simple-eval package <a href="https://github.com/openai/simple-evals" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_url ltx_font_typewriter">https://github.com/openai/simple-evals</a>.</p>
</div>

</span></div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption" style="font-size:80%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 10: </span>
A Comparison of DeepSeek-Coder-V2 Instruct with DeepSeek-V2 Chat.
</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S4.SS6.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS6.p2.1" class="ltx_p">When comparing the performance of 16B models, it is evident that DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite-Instruct outperforms DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat in benchmarks like BBH and Arena-Hard. These benchmarks place a high demand on the model’s reasoning ability, which DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite-Instruct excels at. However, DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite Instruct falls behind in knowledge-intensive benchmarks like TriviaQA, primarily due to the relatively smaller amount of web data used during pre-training.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS6.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS6.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Moving on to 236B models, DeepSeek-Coder-V2 Instruct exhibits greater strength in reasoning benchmarks, particularly in Arena-Hard, which comprises a substantial proportion of code, math, and reasoning questions. On the other hand, DeepSeek-V2 Chat demonstrates slightly better results in benchmarks such as MT-bench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib42" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zheng et al., 2023</a>)</cite>, AlpacaEval 2.0 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">Dubois et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, and AlignBench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2023c</a>)</cite>. This advantage can be attributed to the general-purpose alignment stage of DeepSeek-V2 Chat.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">5 </span>Conclusion</h2>

<div id="S5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this paper, we introduce DeepSeek-Coder-V2 to further advance the field of code intelligence, which is continually pre-trained from DeepSeek-V2 with 6 trillion tokens sourced from a high-quality and multi-source corpus. Through this continued pre-training, we find that DeepSeek-Coder-V2 significantly enhances the model’s capabilities in coding and mathematical reasoning while maintaining comparable general language performance to DeepSeek-V2. Compared to DeepSeek-Coder, DeepSeek-Coder-V2 supports a significantly larger number of programming languages, increasing from 86 to 338, and extends the maximum context length from 16K to 128K tokens. Experimental results demonstrate that DeepSeek-Coder-V2 achieves performance comparable to state-of-the-art closed-source models such as GPT-4 Turbo, Claude 3 Opus, and Gemini 1.5 Pro in code and math-specific tasks.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Although DeepSeek-Coder-V2 achieves impressive performance on standard benchmarks, we find that there is still a significant gap in instruction-following capabilities compared to current state-of-the-art models like GPT-4 Turbo. This gap leads to poor performance in complex scenarios and tasks such as those in SWEbench. Therefore, we believe that a code model needs not only strong coding abilities but also exceptional instruction-following capabilities to handle real-world complex programming scenarios. In the future, we will focus more on improving the model’s instruction-following capabilities to better handle real-world complex programming scenarios and enhance the productivity of the development process.</p>
</div>
</section>
